We need to return all possible precursors of applying the template that was result of make_6_lvl2-template_search-2. The template search failed earlier. But we have a list of templates from search with criteria (halide broken, amide formed). The result includes several templates with IDs (reaction_id). We need to apply the appropriate template to the molecule COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1. Which template corresponds to the Friedel-Crafts acylation? The description: forward reaction is Friedel-Crafts acylation introducing acyl group onto aromatic ring, breaking C-Cl bond (halide). The product is our molecule (has amide attached to aromatic). The precursor likely is an aryl chloride (aryl halide) and an acyl chloride (or acid). The template likely is the one with retro_smarts that breaks C-Cl and forms amide. Look at the templates list: first entry seems weird with large complex SMILES; second entry (reaction_id 1111246) has retro_smarts: '[#7:5]-[C;H0;D3;+0:6](=[O;D1;H0:7])-[c;H0;D3;+0:1](:[#7;a:2]):[c:3]:[#7;a:4]>>Cl-[c;H0;D3;+0:1](:[#7;a:2]):[c:3]:[#7;a:4].[#7:5]-[CH;D2;+0:6]=[O;D1;H0:7]'. This seems to break a C-Cl bond on aromatic (Cl attached to aromatic) and an amide carbonyl to give acyl chloride? Actually the forward direction: Cl-aryl + amide? Wait retro direction: product (amide attached to aromatic) -> precursors: aryl chloride + acyl? The retro_smarts shows product side left? The template is retro: product -> precursors. It shows product pattern: [#7:5]-C(=O)-[c...] (amide attached to aromatic) >> Cl-aryl + [#7:5]-[CH]=O (maybe acyl chloride?). Actually the second part is [#7:5]-[CH;D2;+0:6]=[O;D1;H0:7] which is an amide? That's a carbonyl attached to nitrogen? That's maybe a formamide? Not sure.

But we can apply this template to our molecule using apply_template. Need correct template_id: the template_hash? The tool expects template_id (likely the template_hash). In search result, each entry has 'template_hash'. Use that. For second entry, template_hash = '737ef6d8bf6053068d052a69aa000435f871443ee1f78754713567a58541ac74'. That's what we tried earlier and got error because tool expects integer? Maybe template_id should be reaction_id? The error shows query expecting integer reaction_id. So template_id likely is reaction_id. Let's try with reaction_id 1111246.
